definition: the earthy smell that rises when rain falls on dry ground
example: She opened the window just to breathe in the petrichor after the storm.
hook: That smell after it rains has a name.

definition: the realization that every stranger has a life as vivid and complex as your own
example: Stuck in traffic, he felt a wave of sonder looking at all the other drivers.
hook: You've felt this in traffic and never knew the word.

definition: the act of throwing someone or something out of a window
example: After the update deleted his save file, the defenestration of his laptop felt justified.
hook: There's a word for throwing something out a window. Seriously.

definition: a person who gives opinions on things far outside their knowledge
example: My uncle is an ultracrepidarian about everything from vaccines to rocket science.
hook: There's a perfect word for that one guy in the comments.

definition: buying books and letting them pile up without reading them
example: My nightstand is pure tsundoku: twelve books, zero finished.
hook: If you buy books you never read, this word is about you.

definition: the warmth of the sun on a cold winter day
example: We sat on the bench soaking up the apricity of a January afternoon.
hook: This might be the most beautiful word in English.

definition: a commotion or fuss, usually over something minor
example: There was a huge kerfuffle over who ate the last slice of pizza.
hook: Say this word in your next argument and watch them lose it.

definition: the obsessive, involuntary state of being infatuated with someone
example: He checked her profile twenty times a day, lost in limerence.
hook: That crush you can't stop thinking about? There's a word for it.

definition: a look shared by two people who each want the other to do something neither wants to do first
example: When the check arrived, there was a long moment of mamihlapinatapai.
hook: There's a word for that awkward look when the bill comes.

definition: seeing faces or meaningful shapes in random things, like clouds or outlets
example: Thanks to pareidolia, my toaster always looks a little surprised.
hook: Ever seen a face in an electrical outlet? That has a name.

definition: language that is meaningless or hard to understand, especially jargon
example: The terms and conditions were twelve pages of legal gobbledygook.
hook: The perfect word for every terms and conditions page.

definition: the strange wistfulness of used bookstores
example: Wandering the dusty aisles, she was overcome by vellichor.
hook: That feeling in an old bookstore? Someone named it.

definition: a noisy, overexcited reaction to something
example: The new patch notes caused a brouhaha across the entire community.
hook: This sounds made up but it's a real word.

definition: the inability to remember the word you want to say
example: Mid-presentation, a sudden bout of lethologica left him pointing and saying 'the thing.'
hook: There's a word for forgetting a word. I'm not joking.

definition: characterized by long words; long-winded
example: His sesquipedalian essay used 'utilize' fourteen times.
hook: The word for using big words is itself a huge word.

definition: a deep longing for a home you can't return to, or that maybe never was
example: Hearing the old song filled her with hiraeth for her childhood town.
hook: Homesick for a place that doesn't exist anymore? There's a word.

definition: a shrewd, unprincipled person, especially a politician
example: Only a snollygoster would promise free pizza and then cancel the party.
hook: Bring this insult back. It's too good.

definition: the lights and colors you see when you rub your closed eyes
example: He rubbed his eyes after the long stream and watched the phosphenes swirl.
hook: Those colors when you rub your eyes have a name.

definition: too great or extreme to be expressed in words
example: Beating the final boss after forty tries brought an ineffable joy.
hook: The word for feelings too big for words.

definition: confused and disconcerted
example: Waking up from a nap at 7 p.m. left me completely discombobulated.
hook: You've felt this after a long nap. Here's the word.

definition: a soft whispering or rustling sound
example: The susurrus of the leaves helped her fall asleep.
hook: This word literally sounds like what it means.

definition: pleasure taken from someone else's misfortune
example: Watching the cheater get banned gave everyone a little schadenfreude.
hook: Admit it. You've felt this and liked it.

definition: to confuse or fluster someone
example: The plot twist completely bumfuzzled the audience.
hook: This is a real word and you need to start using it.

definition: relating to a transitional or in-between state or space
example: Empty airports at 3 a.m. have a strange liminal feeling.
hook: Why do empty hallways feel so creepy? This word explains it.

definition: a word that imitates the sound it describes, like buzz or boom
example: Comic books are full of onomatopoeia: pow, bam, whoosh.
hook: Most people can't spell this word. Can you?

definition: the sick feeling from eating or drinking way too much
example: After the all-you-can-eat buffet, crapulence set in.
hook: That Thanksgiving feeling has an official name.

definition: extremely idealistic and unrealistic, chasing impossible dreams
example: His quixotic plan was to speedrun the game blindfolded.
hook: Smart people use this word. Now you can too.

definition: a cloud-walker; someone who lives in their imagination and ignores convention
example: The teacher called her a nefelibata, always dreaming through math class.
hook: If you daydream all the time, this word is you.

definition: lasting for a very short time
example: Fame on the internet is ephemeral; today's meme is tomorrow's cringe.
hook: One word that describes the entire internet.

definition: a harsh, chaotic mixture of sounds
example: The group voice chat was a cacophony of screaming and keyboard clicks.
hook: Your group chat at 2 a.m. in one word.

definition: finding something good by happy accident
example: By pure serendipity, the wrong turn led them to the best taco truck in town.
hook: The best things in life happen because of this word.

definition: to make something deliberately unclear or confusing
example: The company tried to obfuscate the price with hidden fees.
hook: Companies do this to you every single day.

definition: finding beauty in imperfection and impermanence
example: The cracked old mug had a wabi-sabi charm she couldn't throw away.
hook: This idea will change how you see flaws.

definition: lacking sense or intelligence; clueless
example: He stood there with a gormless grin after walking into the glass door.
hook: The politest way to call someone clueless.

definition: sweet and smooth sounding, pleasant to hear
example: The narrator's mellifluous voice made the boring documentary bearable.
hook: One of the most satisfying words to say out loud.

definition: extremely surprised or shocked
example: She was flabbergasted when her first video hit a million views.
hook: How you'll feel when your first video goes viral.

definition: a deep sense of flourishing and living a meaningful life
example: For him, eudaimonia meant building things with his own hands.
hook: The ancient Greek secret to happiness in one word.

definition: lacking enthusiasm and effort; lazily careless
example: His lackadaisical defense let the other team score three times.
hook: The fancy way to say someone isn't even trying.

definition: something placed in the wrong time period
example: A smartphone in a medieval movie would be an obvious anachronism.
hook: Movies get caught making this mistake all the time.

definition: a feeling of listless boredom and dissatisfaction
example: Sunday evening ennui hit hard as the weekend slipped away.
hook: That Sunday night feeling has a French name.
